title: US Reserve Balances Edge Higher to $2.96T, Signaling Slight Liquidity Uptick
body: Reserve balances held with Federal Reserve Banks in the United States rose to $2.962 trillion, up from the previous level of $2.895 trillion, according to the latest data updated on 5 November 2026. The move marks a modest increase in aggregate reserves in the banking system. The uptick in reserve balances suggests a mild expansion in liquidity parked at the Fed, which can reflect shifts in banks' demand for reserves or the central bank's balance sheet dynamics. While the change is not dramatic in absolute terms, the nearly $70 billion rise may be closely watched by market participants looking for signals on funding conditions and the broader monetary environment. Investors and analysts are likely to monitor whether this increase in reserves becomes a sustained trend or proves temporary, as reserve levels can influence short-term interest rates, bank funding costs, and overall financial conditions in the U.S. economy. title: Fed Balance Sheet Edges Higher to $6.748 Trillion, Signaling Ongoing Cautious Stance
body: The U.S. Federal Reserve's balance sheet has inched up to $6,748 billion, according to data updated on 5 November 2026, from a previous level of $6,746 billion. The modest $2 billion increase suggests that the Fed is maintaining a largely steady stance in managing its asset holdings. While the move is small in absolute terms, even marginal changes in the balance sheet are closely watched by markets for clues about the central bank's approach to liquidity and broader financial conditions. The latest figure indicates that the Fed is neither aggressively expanding nor rapidly shrinking its portfolio, underscoring a measured approach as policymakers navigate the current economic backdrop. Investors and economists will continue to monitor upcoming releases for signs of any shift in the pace or direction of balance sheet adjustments, which can influence market expectations for interest rates and financial stability. title: Oil Rises as Middle East Supply Risks Persist
body: Crude oil prices rose on Thursday for the first time in four sessions, climbing nearly 3% to about $90.50 a barrel after having slumped more than 8% to a near two-month low in the previous session. Market participants are weighing whether the Democratic Party's gains in the US midterm elections might improve the outlook for a diplomatic settlement to the dispute with Iran. Tehran is reviewing proposals conveyed via regional intermediaries, though significant differences between Washington and Tehran persist over the terms of any potential deal. At the same time, shipping risks remain elevated. Since Sunday, at least five vessel-related incidents have been reported in the Persian Gulf, and threats to commercial traffic continue despite a rebound in crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Supply conditions have improved markedly, with Gulf crude exports recovering toward pre-war levels, albeit at higher transportation costs. Even so, the geopolitical risks surrounding these flows remain unresolved. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Mexican Peso Retreats as Banxico Eases Monetary Policy
body: The Mexican peso weakened to around 18.8 per US dollar after Banxico cut its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.25% at its November 2026 meeting, contrary to market expectations for no change. The central bank stated that the disinflation process was ongoing and assessed that existing economic slack would limit the pass-through from exchange rate movements to consumer prices. It also signaled that keeping rates at this new level for an extended period would support inflation's convergence toward its target while helping to address external macroeconomic challenges. At the same time, the narrower interest rate differential between Banxico and the US Federal Reserve has reduced the appeal of peso-denominated carry trades, putting further pressure on the currency. The peso also gave back part of the gains made after the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections, as markets interpreted the result as a potential constraint on the Trump administration's ability to maintain elevated tariffs on foreign trade. title: Banxico Delivers Unexpected Rate Cut
body: At its November 2026 meeting, Banxico cut its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.25%, contrary to market expectations of no change. The Governing Board reported that the disinflation process continued and assessed that, given the prevailing slack in the economy, recent exchange rate movements would have only a limited pass-through to consumer prices. It also underscored the absence of demand-driven inflationary pressures and emphasized that the already-implemented monetary tightening remained in effect. Looking ahead, the Board signaled that keeping the policy rate at its new level for an extended period would support the convergence of inflation toward its target and help Mexico navigate external macroeconomic challenges. At the same time, Banxico revised its headline inflation forecast upward for Q4 2026 and adjusted its core inflation projection slightly higher. Nevertheless, headline inflation is still expected to converge to the 3% target by Q4 2027. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Bank of Mexico Eases Policy Rate to 6.25% in November Move
body: Mexico's central bank cut its key interest rate to 6.25% in November 2026, lowering borrowing costs from the previous level of 6.50% last set in September 2026, according to data updated on 5 November 2026. The decision marks a continuation of Mexico's monetary easing cycle, with policymakers opting for a 0.25 percentage point reduction in the benchmark rate. The previous rate of 6.50% had been maintained since September, before the latest adjustment brought the indicator down to 6.25% in November. The new level suggests that authorities are seeking to provide additional support to economic activity while navigating the balance between inflation control and growth. Market participants will be watching subsequent rate decisions and data releases closely to gauge the central bank's next steps and the trajectory of Mexican monetary policy heading into the end of 2026. title: Brazil 10-Year Yield Extends 10-Year High
body: Brazil's 10-year government bond yield was steady around 15.29%, hovering near its highest level in a decade after the central bank (BCB) left the Selic rate unchanged at 13.75% at its November meeting. The decision reflected an outlook of weaker economic growth, higher inflation, and elevated uncertainty following President Lula's reelection. Markets remain focused on fiscal policy, especially the government's willingness and ability to rein in spending and stabilize public debt, which has climbed sharply in recent years. Ahead of the meeting, expectations were split: some investors anticipated a pause, while others were pricing in a sixth straight 25 bps rate cut. Policymakers pointed to rising inflation expectations, greater uncertainty, and a "more pronounced deceleration" in economic activity. The Copom statement underscored both the economic slowdown and the increased uncertainty surrounding its own projections. Labor market figures reinforced signs of cooling: Brazil generated 121,305 formal jobs in September, well below market forecasts of 171,000. title: TSX Falls on Global Technology Selloff
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index dropped more than 2%, slipping below 36,000 points, as a broad selloff in US semiconductor and AI-related names spilled over into Canadian technology stocks. The pullback wiped out the previous session's post-midterm election rally, with Democratic gains in the US midterms heightening worries about tighter regulatory oversight on the rapid growth of artificial intelligence. Celestica slumped 14%, while Shopify fell more than 5.5%, mirroring sharp losses in US chipmakers and hyperscalers. Financials also came under pressure: major banks traded lower as a rebound in oil prices reignited concerns over energy-driven inflation. RBC, BMO, and CIBC each declined about 2%, and Scotiabank and TD Bank shed more than 2.5%. On the earnings front, Canadian Natural inched higher after posting third-quarter profits that topped expectations, supported by firmer crude prices and increased production. Nutrien rose about 1% despite missing earnings estimates, as Democratic advances in the US elections bolstered hopes for renewed US–Canada trade talks. title: Brazilian Stocks Decline Amid Unfavorable External Backdrop
body: The Ibovespa fell 0.5% to below 168,000 points, reversing earlier gains as a sharp selloff on Wall Street weighed on global equity markets. Shares of companies tied to semiconductors and data centers came under pressure after Democratic gains in the US midterm elections fueled concerns about tighter regulation of the rapid expansion of AI. At the same time, investors remained focused on Brazil's fiscal outlook, particularly the government's commitment to reining in public spending and debt, which have risen sharply in recent years. The BCB left the Selic rate unchanged at 13.75% at its November meeting, against a challenging backdrop of weaker growth, higher inflation, and heightened uncertainty following President Lula's reelection. Losses were broad-based, led by WEG (-4%) and Embraer (-5%), while Petrobras and Bradesco each slipped 1%. In contrast, Vale advanced nearly 1%, supported by higher iron ore prices. title: Wall Street Slides as Chipmakers Tumble
body: The S&P 500 slumped about 3.5%, the Nasdaq sank more than 5%, and the Dow lost nearly 1,500 points on Thursday, erasing the prior session's gains amid a sharp, post-election selloff in semiconductor stocks. The chip sector was on track for its worst weekly performance since the April 2025 tariff-driven rout. Democrats secured control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the midterm elections and are expected to pursue tighter regulations on computing hubs critical to AI development. Market participants fear such measures could slow infrastructure buildouts and delay deployments that major companies are relying on to drive earnings growth. Losses were broad-based across the market, but chipmakers bore the brunt of the decline. Nvidia and AMD each dropped more than 7%, while Micron slid over 12.5%. Tesla also tumbled more than 11%, Applied Materials fell more than 11%, and Lam Research sank more than 13%. Among the hyperscalers, Microsoft declined more than 2.5%, Meta lost over 3.5%, and Oracle plunged 7%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Soybean futures hit oversold territory ahead of USDA report.
body: Soybean futures closed at their lowest levels since August, dipping into extreme oversold territory as the Relative Strength Index fell below 20%. Prices also settled convincingly beneath the 200-day moving average. Meanwhile, weekly export sales reached 1.456 million metric tons, landing below high-end expectations. Markets now look ahead to Tuesday's USDA report for critical updates on national yield, production, and ending stocks as the harvest concludes.

title: Live Cattle futures slide as cash rates and export sales drop.
body: Live Cattle futures experienced a solid slide, with the December contract nearing September lows and the relative strength index dropping to 28%. Cash rates also moved sharply lower, falling $10 over the week. Turbulence in the equity markets added pressure, raising concerns about consumer demand for high-priced beef following large stock market reversals. Meanwhile, weekly export sales remained lackluster at 11,000 metric tons, unchanged from the prior week and down 29% from the four-week average, surprising traders given the lower price environment.
